mainEntity.name: Are flexible dentures more likely to cause sore gums than rigid dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flexible dentures are not inherently more likely to cause sore gums, but they can present different challenges. The pliable material may flex during chewing, creating localised pressure areas that change with use. Rigid acrylic dentures distribute forces more predictably, though they may feel less comfortable initially. Both types require a good fit and regular maintenance. The likelihood of gum soreness depends more on the accuracy of the fit, how well the denture is cared for, and changes in the underlying bone and gum tissue over time than on the material alone.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for gums to adjust to new flexible dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is common for gums to need a short adjustment period when new flexible dentures are first fitted. Mild tenderness or slight discomfort during the first one to two weeks is not unusual as the oral tissues adapt to the new appliance. Our guide on why flexible dentures feel uncomfortable at first covers this adjustment period in more detail. During this time, eating softer foods and following your dental team's advice can help. If soreness persists beyond this initial period, or if specific sore spots develop, it is advisable to contact your dental practice for a review appointment. The denture may need a minor adjustment to relieve any pressure points.

mainEntity.name: Can I use denture adhesive with flexible dentures to reduce soreness?

acceptedAnswer.text: Denture adhesive is not typically recommended for use with flexible dentures, as these appliances are designed to achieve retention through their close adaptation to the gum tissue. If a flexible denture feels loose or is causing soreness due to movement, adhesive may mask an underlying fitting problem rather than resolve it. A better approach is to have the denture assessed by a dental professional who can evaluate whether relining, adjustment, or replacement is appropriate. Using adhesive without addressing the root cause may delay necessary treatment.

mainEntity.name: How often should flexible dentures be replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single fixed timeline for replacing flexible dentures, as their lifespan depends on factors including the rate of bone resorption, the care and maintenance of the denture, and general wear. However, most dental professionals recommend having dentures assessed regularly and potentially replaced every five to eight years, depending on clinical findings. The fit of any denture changes gradually as the jawbone remodels, and what was once a comfortable fit may become a source of irritation. Regular dental reviews help determine the right time for replacement.

mainEntity.name: Can sore gums from dentures lead to more serious problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prolonged gum irritation from an ill-fitting denture can potentially contribute to more significant oral health concerns if left unaddressed. Chronic irritation may lead to persistent inflammation, tissue changes, or recurring infections such as denture stomatitis. In rare cases, long-standing irritation of the oral mucosa warrants further investigation to rule out other conditions. This is one of the reasons why regular dental examinations are important for denture wearers. Early identification and management of gum soreness can help maintain healthy oral tissues and overall comfort.

mainEntity.name: Should I stop wearing my flexible dentures if my gums are sore?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your gums are significantly sore, it may be helpful to remove your dentures for extended rest periods to allow the tissue to recover. However, removing dentures for prolonged periods without professional advice could allow the remaining teeth to shift position, which may affect the denture fit further. The most appropriate course of action is to contact your dental practice for guidance. Your clinician can advise whether temporary removal is suitable and arrange an appointment to examine the cause of the soreness and recommend an appropriate solution.
